attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. He restates and endorses his January 2024 view. The quoted tweets from Burkov, Nik and Zitron are context, not his claim.

semantics.note: Faithful. The claim is a structural causal one: products are interchangeable, so no LLM firm can have a moat. The qualifier 'everybody building the same thing' is kept. The scope is mainly OpenAI and the chatbot market, which the contract flags.

contract.note: The core plain reading is fair and ordinary: no durable advantage, free switching, the leader's share eroding. Treating partial stickiness as evidence against an absolute 'no moat' is fair. Counting Google's ecosystem distribution against him is a stretch, because his claim is about the shared LLM product. The outcome does not depend on that clause.

evidence.note: Sensor Tower, as TechRadar reports, finds low chatbot loyalty and users ready to migrate. This fits 'no moat'. It also names capabilities and ecosystem as reasons to switch, which weakens the 'same thing' cause.
Similarweb, via OfficeChai: ChatGPT's share of web traffic fell from 76.4% to 52.7% in the year to May 2026 as rivals gained. This is May 2026 data, within the target period.
ChatGPT is still the clear leader, with more than 1.1B MAU, despite similar rivals. That is partial evidence of a lasting advantage, against the absolute 'no moat'.
ChatGPT's DAU/MAU has historically been nearly double Gemini's, which suggests more habitual use. That is partial stickiness. The period is not dated precisely, so this is weak counterevidence.

reviews.rationale: What holds: independent share data show ChatGPT losing large share (76% to 53% on Similarweb, under 50% on Sensor Tower), and Sensor Tower reports low loyalty. That fits 'no moat'. What fails: ChatGPT stays the clear leader with more than 1.1B MAU and more habitual users, which is partial stickiness against the absolute claim. The evidence also does not show that sameness of products is the cause: switching is tied to capabilities, ecosystem, pricing and politics. Mixed under any fair reading.
